title: Elastic fibrillae act as a microscopic skeleton shaping spiral cells

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Elastic fibrillae act as a microscopic skeleton shaping spiral cells

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The spiral and other peculiar forms of decapod sperm-cells and of many Infusoria are produced by more or less elastic fibrillae in the cell, which restrain and modify the surface forces like the wire frames and coils in Plateau's experiments, acting as a microscopic skeleton.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In all probability we must in like manner attribute the peculiar spiral and other forms, for instance of many Infusoria, to the presence, among the multitudinous other differentiations of their protoplasmic substance, of such more or less elastic fibrillae, which play as it were the part of a microscopic skeleton

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Osmotic shapes of sperm-cells”. Scope: Infusoria, decapod sperm-cells and other cells with non-equilibrium shapes

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-26: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern cytoskeletal measurements provide a plausible operationalization of 'elastic fibrillae.' Open ultrastructure can test spatial association for selected cells, but causal restraint and mechanical properties usually require new perturbations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Co-register cell shape with internal fibril ultrastructure and test whether fibril position, orientation, and elasticity predict spiral form better than membrane forces alone.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Elasticity is not inferable reliably from fixed ultrastructure.

Sparse taxonomic coverage limits the broad generalization.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Electron microscopy of Paramecium, Tetrahymena and some crustacean sperm can test whether odd outlines are braced by fibrils. The mechanical claim, that those fibrils are elastic restraints equivalent to Plateau's wires, needs perturbation or stiffness data that are not archived for the stated groups. Existing images therefore cover a structural proxy for a few species.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map intracellular fibrils onto the spiral or other non-equilibrium outline of decapod sperm and ciliates, and ask whether the outline relaxes when those fibrils are absent. A fibrillar scaffold whose geometry matches the departure from a surface-tension figure would support the claim; the same outlines without such fibrils, or fibrils that do not follow the spiral, would weaken it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Nearly all of these cells have a cytoskeleton, so presence alone does not show that the fibrils act as Plateau frames.

Cortex and sperm ultrastructure are spread across individual papers, with quantitative shape-versus-fibril tables for only a few model ciliates.
